claims.text: The refractory HEAs NbMoTaW and WTaMoNbV have melting points above 2000 K.
Experimental thermodynamic data are sparse for multi-component refractory HEAs.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput calculations can rapidly screen large HEA composition spaces for phase stability.
CALPHAD screening can provide approximate melting ranges for multi-component HEAs.
An MLIP trained on DFT data from elemental, binary, and ternary subsystems can capture the chemical interactions needed for higher-component HEAs.
Moment tensor potentials can provide near-DFT accuracy with a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost in MoNbTaW.
MLIP-based molecular dynamics can accurately calculate melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity for refractory HEAs.
Chemical short-range order and local atomic environments significantly affect phonon spectra and anharmonic behavior in refractory HEAs.
An MoNbTaW MTP can represent variations associated with local atomic environments and different degrees of short-range order.
MLIPs accurately model anharmonic lattice vibrations in multi-component HEAs.
MLIPs accurately capture configurational-entropy contributions to thermal properties.
CALPHAD supplies thermodynamically consistent equilibrium predictions across multi-component composition space.
Incomplete thermodynamic databases cause standard CALPHAD methods to struggle with accurate melting-point prediction in multi-component systems.
Standard CALPHAD models cannot adequately capture anharmonic effects.
Direct DFT is too computationally expensive for screening vast HEA composition spaces.
Conventional empirical potentials lack sufficient accuracy for complex multi-component interactions.
The hybrid framework can predict HEA melting temperatures within ±50 K.
The hybrid framework can predict HEA entropy of fusion within ±10%.
The hybrid framework can accurately predict heat-capacity trends across HEA composition variations.

The framework is valid for single-phase solid solutions with moderate short-range order but may fail for strong long-range ordering, complex intermetallic formation, non-equilibrium states, or configurations outside its training domain.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify a compositional space with 5 or more principal elements, but NbMoTaW, a principal example in the initial state, contains only four named elements.
